name: Daemon, Voragodaemon
body:
Voragodaemon
CR 17

This red, sinewy fiend looks through its cunning blue eyes over a set of sharp, needle-like teeth. Its back is covered in sharp, bony appendages and each of its hands ends in a set of three claws, each the length of a shortsword and covered in a soft, violet glow.

XP 102,400
NE Huge outsider (daemon, evil, extraplanar)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 120 ft., detect good, greater arcane sight, true seeing Perception +31; Aura soul siphon (100 ft.), unholy aura (DC 22)

DEFENSE

AC 35, touch 14, flat-footed 33 (+4 deflection, +2 Dex, +21 natural, -2 size)
hp 279 (18d10+180); fast healing 10
Fort +20, Ref +17, Will +17
DR 10/good or silver; Immune acid, death effects, disease, poison; Resist cold 10, electricity 10, fire 10; SR 28

OFFENSE

Speed 5 ft., fly 50 ft. (perfect)
Melee bite +30 (2d8+19/19-20 plus energy drain and grab)
Ranged soulsear ray +18 touch (10d6 negative energy plus energy drain)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks death gaze, energy drain (2 levels, DC 25) swallow whole (4d8+19 bludgeoning plus energy drain, AC 20, hp 27)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 18th; concentration +22)

Constant—detect good, greater arcane sight, true seeing, unholy aura (DC 22)
At will—confusion (DC 18), greater teleport (self plus 50 lbs. objects only), telekinesis (DC 19), invisibility, fireball (DC 17)
3/day—delayed blast fireball (DC 21), feeblemind (DC 19)
1/day—summon (level 8, 1 voragodaemon 50%), wail of the banshee (DC 23)

STATISTICS

Str 36, Dex 15, Con 30, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 19
Base Atk +18; CMB +33 (+37 grapple); CMD 49
Feats Ability Focus (death gaze, energy drain), Greater Vital Strike, Improved Critical (bite), Improved Initiative, Improved Vital Strike, Power Attack, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Appraise +23, Fly +27, Intimidate +25, Knowledge (arcana, planes) +23, Perception +31, Spellcraft +23, Stealth +15; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception
Languages Abyssal, Common, Infernal; telepathy 100 ft.

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Death Gaze (Su)

1d4 negative levels, 30 feet; Fortitude DC 25 negates. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Soulsear Ray (Su)

A voragodaemon can shoot a soul-rending ray from its eye as a standard action. This is a ranged touch attack with a range of 100 feet and no range increment.

Soul Siphon (Su)

If any creature within 100 feet of a voragodaemon is reduced to negative hit points, it is immediately slain. This is a death effect. The soul of every creature dying within 100 feet of a voragodaemon is siphoned into its maw. Whenever a soul is siphoned in this way, the voragodaemon’s fast healing is doubled and it gains the effects of haste for a number of rounds equal to half the siphoned soul’s Hit Dice. The siphoned soul is immediately imprisoned in a gem, which rapidly grows out of voragodaemon’s hide. This works as soul bind, except the gem itself is worthless. A voragodaemon can hold any number of such soul gems on itself, although for every 10 gems growing out of its hide, it gains a +1 bonus to its natural armor and a -1 penalty to its Dexterity. A voragodaemon whose Dexterity reaches 0 as a result of this ability may still accrue gems, although it is immobile as a result of its Dexterity score. A voragodaemon can shed any number of gems as a free action. Soul gems can be removed from an unwilling voragodaemon’s hide with a steal combat maneuver.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (Abaddon)
Organization solitary, pair, or harvest (3-12)
Treasure standard

The voragodaemon is a new addition to the ancient ranks of daemonkind, and one that first spawned artificially. Created by the most powerful of daemons as a next step in the industrialization of soul trade, voragodaemons came into being from eon-spanning series of experiments aimed at crafting an evolutionary next step of a cacodaemon. This project partially succeeded. While voragodaemons are extremely potent soul harvesters, they’re too powerful to be easily controlled and too rare to outpace the hard work of cacodaemon throngs. While originally created via a secret, arduous process, voragodaemons are now rumored to spawn from souls killed by energy drain, similar to astradaemons, key difference being that voragodaemons form specifically from powerful spellcasters that meet such fate.

A voragodaemon siphons souls passively, creating a coat out of shimmering soul gems it grows on its body and then shedding them at will. While such an ability would indeed be invaluable at one of Abaddon’s slave processing plants, such is a voragodaemon’s power that it is more likely to run the location in the first place, refusing to be shackled into the role of a perpetually gem-encumbered soulgrinder. It is much more likely for a voragodaemon to aid a powerful evil being by hovering, silent and invisible, over a raid or a place of battle organized by their ally, quickly growing a dense crust of solidified soulstuff to fill the vault of their partner or master.

In combat, voragodaemons are a formidable foe, every part of their arsenal attacking not only body, but soul. Jaws and stomachs of these fiends tear vital energy of their victims just as they tear at their flesh. Their great, cyclopean eye rends souls with its very gaze, and is able to shoot out rays of negative, enervating energy. This same eye grants them unparallelled senses, including an ability to effortlessly identify magic and pierce illusions. Voragodaemons resemble their pathetic forebears in general appearance, although they are notably more menacing, with a glowing, red eye, spiky growths and powerful, bony armor. They are also quite massive, easily reaching 20 feet or more in diameter and weighing 15 tons.
